editorial.headline: Aircraft Maintenance, Including Drones, Is Foreign-Open in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 33153 covers approved aircraft maintenance work, with national PMA access up to 100% and no Bali moratorium block in the slim record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 33153 is a maintenance code for aviation work. Its centre of gravity is the repair and upkeep of aircraft, including drones, aircraft engines, and aircraft equipment. That makes it a technical service category rather than a manufacturing or rebuilding category: the slim record expressly excludes alteration, inspection, and rebuilding of aircraft and aircraft engines. In plain English, this is where an approved maintenance organisation would sit when its business is keeping aircraft or aviation equipment serviceable, not remaking them.

The record is unusually broad on business scale. It is open to micro, small, medium, and large operators, which matters because aircraft maintenance is not always a single kind of company. Some registrants may be highly specialised maintenance outfits; others may be larger approved maintenance organisations with broader capability across aircraft, drones, engines, and associated equipment. The common thread is the activity itself: repair and maintenance within the stated scope, carried out as an aircraft maintenance organisation.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clean. The PMA status is open, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. That national position is sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no partial foreign cap in the slim record, so the editorial conclusion should not soften that point: at the national level, this activity is open to full foreign ownership according to the data provided.

Bali does not reverse that outcome in this record. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the Bali block flag is false. The reason is specific: at large scale, the OSS risk sits at medium-high/high, so it is not caught by Bali’s moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record blocks all low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, permanently, but this activity is not blocked on the facts supplied here. The honest Bali reading is therefore straightforward: a foreign-owned setup can look at this activity as nationally open and not moratorium-blocked in Bali, while keeping the registration aligned to the precise maintenance scope described above.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest Bali reading is straightforward: this activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership and is not moratorium-blocked in the record.
